parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian охотиник (oxotinik). By surface analysis, ahotă + -nic.
From alb + gardist. Calque of Russian белогвардеец (belogvardejec).

parole.significato: synonym of alo (word used to answer the telephone)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian анархосиндикалист (anarxosindikalist). By surface analysis, anarho- + sindicalist.

Borrowed from Russian бахмать (baxmatʹ) or Ukrainian бахмать (baxmatʹ).

parole.significato: illegal activity, particularly travelling on a train without a ticket.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian блат (blat, “cronyism”), from Polish blat (“the flat surface of a table”) or Yiddish בלאַט (blat), from German Blatt, from Middle High German blat, plat, from Old High German blat, from Proto-West Germanic *blad (“leaf”), from Proto-Germanic *bladą (“leaf”).
Borrowed from Russian блин (blin), from Proto-Slavic *mlinъ.

parole.significato: liquid fermented wheat or barley bran
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian борщ (boršč) or Ukrainian борщ (boršč), from Proto-Slavic *bъrščь.
Borrowed from Russian брак (brak), from Polish brak, ultimately from Middle Low German brak (“flaw, defect; breaking”); Compare modern German Bruch and English break.
Borrowed from Russian брага (braga), from Proto-Slavic *braga.
Borrowed from Russian бума́жка (bumážka), a diminutive of бума́га (bumága).
Borrowed from Russian буржуй (buržuj), from French bourgeois.

Borrowed from Russian бутафорский (butaforskij). By surface analysis, butaforie + -ic.

Borrowed from Russian каре́та (karéta), itself from Polish kareta, from Italian carretta.

parole.significato: to quarter, to garrison, to lodge
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian квартировать (kvartirovatʹ), from квартира (kvartira), from Latin quartarius.

parole.significato: knight (warrior, especially of the Middle Ages)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian кавале́р (kavalér), from French cavalier, Italian cavaliere.

parole.significato: member of a society or a courthouse

Borrowed from Russian колхозник (kolxoznik). By surface analysis, colhoz + -nic.

parole.significato: bill of a cap, brim, peak

Borrowed from Russian курган (kurgan). Doublet of gorgan.

Borrowed from Russian генеалогияский (genealogijaskij). Equivalent to genealogic + -esc or genealogie + -icesc.

Borrowed from Russian геологический (geologičeskij). By surface analysis, geologie + -icesc or geologic + -esc.

Borrowed from Russian горнист (gornist). Equivalent to goarnă + -ist.

parole.significato: police officer, policeman, militsia officer (during the Soviet period and in some post-Soviet successor states)

Borrowed from Russian морфоструктура (morfostruktura). By surface analysis, morfo- + structură.

parole.significato: vertical board on a fishing boat, used to prevent fish from sliding into the bottom of the boat

parole.significato: explanation (the act or process of explaining)

Borrowed from Russian оппортунизм (opportunizm). Equivalent to oportun + -ism.

Borrowed from Russian плита (plita) or Ukrainian плита (plyta).

Borrowed from Russian пожарник (požarnik). By surface analysis, pojar + -nic.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian шафра́н (šafrán), Polish szafran.

Borrowed from Russian царевич (carevič), from царь (carʹ) + -евич (-evič), from Old East Slavic цьсарь (cĭsarĭ), from цѣсарь (cěsarĭ), from Proto-Slavic *cěsařь, from a Germanic language, from Proto-Germanic *kaisaraz, from Latin Caesar.
